text:
talia: Noticing a correlated spike in WS reconnects and duplicate session counts for a few big tenants (EU & APAC) starting ~02:15 UTC. Looks like clients trigger reconnects before resume arrives.

sam: any logs or packet snippets? sounds similar to previous SSE fragment case but on websockets.

talia: pasted an edge trace (redacted):
```
PROXY: write frame(id=xyz, len=18, coalesced=true)
PROXY: forwarded
CLIENT: recv ping (partial)
CLIENT: heartbeat timeout -> reconnect
PROXY: later flush remainder frame(id=xyz, len=70)
PROXY: resume token x-rtk-... included in later fragment
```

ravi: coalesced=true stands out. our socket write coalescer batches small frames for throughput; if the resume token lands in the second write and client treats the first as a complete ping, they reconnect. Resume dedupe then fails because Last-Event-ID/token wasn't visible at reconnect time.

ops-jen: console is showing these as two separate sessions (new + resumed) which inflates billing and alarms. We need a short-term mitigation and longer-term fix.

pm-lee: monitor-bot, can you show the query that triggered the alert?

monitor-bot: alert: websocket-reconnect-rate (route=prefer-low-latency) > 4x baseline in eu-west (last 15m). sample_count=258.

sam: quick mitigation options: 1) mark coalesced writes with a telemetry tag and surface in console; 2) ensure resume metadata is copied to the first buffered fragment when coalescing; 3) small client-side compatibility doc asking integrators to tolerate partial pings.

ravi: technical note: copying resume metadata to the first fragment is easiest in proxy coalescer. we already have fragment metadata for SSE; need same for WS frames. also add a per-connection 'pending-resume' flag so reconnect path can check server-side dedupe even if token missing briefly.

ops-jen: for console UX: add a "coalesced-frame" filter to the reconnects panel and a new timeseries for "duplicate-session-rate". also a banner to explain false-duplicate-count for affected time window.

pm-lee: schedule: - hotfix telemetry tagging today - proxy patch to copy resume metadata + unit tests by EOD - staging integration tonight - canary in eu-west + ap-sg for 6h tomorrow morning.

sam: also propose a short grace-window on client-side heartbeat detection: treat missing pong for 200ms as tolerated when coalesced-frame=true. but we can't force clients to change; better to put grace logic in proxy where we can detect coalescing.

ravi: implementing grace in proxy: hold client heartbeat-notify for 200ms if coalesced flag present OR if last write flagged as "maybe-incomplete". code sketch: 
```
if (coalesced_frame) {
  scheduleHeartbeatCheck(delay=200ms)
} else {
  scheduleHeartbeatCheck(delay=default)
}
```

ops-jen: agree on proxy-side grace. we'll avoid client docs for now.

pm-lee: ops ask: can console avoid counting resumed connections as new sessions until server-side dedupe probe completes? i.e., delay billing counter by 1s for resumed flows if resume metadata appears shortly after connect.

sam: we can emit a "session-provisional" state in telemetry for up to 1s; billing pipeline can then fold events if resume_token shows up. need to ensure not to undercount legitimate new sessions. suggest gate via feature flag per-tenant.

monitor-bot: notice: created metric "ws.coalesced_frame" and spike chart added.

talia: initial temporary remediation: enabling "session-provisional" for tenants cust-77 and cust-201 reduced duplicate counts by ~70% in last 20m.

ravi: follow-ups: - add unit/integration tests that simulate split-frame resume token - add e2e test for billing foldback with provisional state - copy resume metadata into coalesced head fragment - add sampling of raw frame headers (PII-free) for debugging.

ops-jen: I'll file console + billing tickets and roll the panel change. pm-lee can you coordinate comms if customers ask?

pm-lee: noted. will prepare a short incident blurb and include mitigations.

sam: I'll open PR 'ws/coalesce-resume-fix' and include tests. Ravi, can you review?

ravi: will review. plan to push to staging after tests.

talia: thanks team. will continue to monitor and report if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
